meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 3 (Multi-Select): Server Features (Tools, Resources, Prompts)
meta.format: multi_select: questions use the 'answers' array (multiple correct options). Some include an 'All of the above' option that is only correct when every other option is.

questions.question: Which method/primitive pairings are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: tools/list and tools/call for tools
resources/list, resources/templates/list, and resources/read for resources
prompts/list and prompts/get for prompts
prompts/call for executing prompts
resources/write for updating resources

questions.explanation: Tools are discovered and executed (list/call); resources are listed, template-listed, and read (read-only); prompts are listed and retrieved with prompts/get. There is no prompts/call or resources/write.

questions.question: Which fields appear in a tool definition returned by tools/list? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: name — the unique identifier within the server's namespace
title — a human-readable display name
description — what the tool does and when to use it
inputSchema — a JSON Schema for the expected parameters
transport — the transport the tool requires

questions.explanation: Tool objects carry name, title, description, and inputSchema (optionally an outputSchema). Transport is a connection-level concern, not per-tool metadata.

questions.question: Which statements about resources are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Each resource has a unique URI and declares a MIME type
Direct resources use fixed URIs; resource templates use parameterized URIs like weather://forecast/{city}/{date}
Resource templates support parameter completion
Resources are model-controlled: the LLM decides when to fetch them
Watching a resource for changes uses subscriptions/listen with a resourceSubscriptions filter

questions.explanation: Resources are application-driven (the host decides retrieval and usage), not model-controlled — that's tools. Everything else is accurate, including the 2026-07-28 subscription mechanism.

questions.question: Which human-oversight mechanisms do the docs suggest applications implement around tools? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Displaying available tools in the UI so users can scope what's available
Approval dialogs for individual tool executions
Permission settings for pre-approving certain safe operations
Activity logs showing tool executions with their results
A mandatory cooling-off delay before any tool runs

questions.explanation: The four suggested mechanisms are UI visibility, per-execution approval, pre-approval permissions, and activity logs. No mandatory delay exists in the protocol or guidance.

questions.question: Match the interaction model: which pairings are correct per the spec? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Tools are model-controlled — the LLM decides when to invoke them (with user approval)
Resources are application-controlled — the host decides when to fetch and use them
Prompts are user-controlled — explicitly selected, e.g., as slash commands
Prompts are model-controlled — the LLM injects them automatically
All of the above

questions.explanation: The control triad is tools→model, resources→application, prompts→user. D contradicts C, so 'All of the above' is a trap.

questions.question: Which fields can a resource returned by resources/list carry? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: uri — the unique identifier
name and title
mimeType
ttlMs and cacheScope on the surrounding list result
All of the above

questions.explanation: Resources carry uri, name/title, description, and mimeType, and since SEP-2549 the list result itself is a CacheableResult with ttlMs and cacheScope. Everything listed is true.

questions.question: Which statements about tools/call results are correct in 2026-07-28? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The result carries a required resultType field
resultType: "input_required" signals an MRTR interim result whose inputRequests need answering
A tool failure is reported with isError rather than a JSON-RPC protocol error
resultType: "task" is reserved for the Tasks extension
All of the above

questions.explanation: All four are accurate: resultType is mandatory (SEP-2322), input_required drives MRTR, execution failures use isError inside the result, and 'task' is reserved for io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks.

questions.question: Which statements about tool naming and schemas are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A tool's name must be unique within its server's namespace
inputSchema is JSON Schema; since SEP-2106 any JSON Schema 2020-12 keywords are allowed
On Streamable HTTP, the called tool's name is mirrored in the Mcp-Name header
Two servers connected to one host may not expose tools with the same name
All of the above

questions.explanation: Name uniqueness is per server — collisions across servers are the host's problem to disambiguate, so D is false and E falls with it.

questions.question: Which statements about tool-result content blocks are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A single result may mix multiple block types (e.g., text plus an image)
Image and audio blocks carry base64 data with a mimeType
A resource link lets the client fetch large data on demand instead of inlining it
Every result must contain exactly one text block
All of the above

questions.explanation: Results are arrays — mixing types is the point, and there's no exactly-one-text-block rule (structured-only or media-only results are fine).

questions.question: Which of the following are methods used to interact with server primitives?

options.text: tools/list
resources/read
prompts/get
tools/execute

questions.explanation: The valid methods are tools/list, resources/read, and prompts/get. There is no tools/execute method - tools are invoked via tools/call.

questions.question: Which statements about the control model are correct?

options.text: Tools are controlled by the model (LLM decides)
Resources are controlled by the application (host decides)
Prompts are controlled by the user (explicit selection)
All three primitives are controlled by the server

questions.explanation: Tools = model-controlled, Resources = application-controlled, Prompts = user-controlled. The server exposes primitives but does not control who uses them.

questions.question: Which scenarios demonstrate correct use of the control model?

options.text: User types /summarize to trigger a prompt
Model decides to call get_weather to answer a question
Host automatically includes project README as context
Server sends a notification to the client

questions.explanation: /summarize is user-controlled (Prompt), get_weather is model-controlled (Tool), README is application-controlled (Resource). Server notifications are not part of the control model.

questions.question: What are the two interaction paradigms in the control model?

options.text: DO - model executes actions
IS - model reads information
RUN - server processes requests
GET - client retrieves data

questions.explanation: The control model has two paradigms: DO (model executes actions via Tools) and IS (model reads information via Resources). RUN and GET are not official terms.
